questions.stem: Fund A value starts from Rs. 40000 and Fund B value starts from Rs. 20000. Their successive changes are +10%, -10% and +15%, +15% respectively. Find the difference between the final values.
questions.explanation:
For Fund A value first stage, increase = 10%. So the new value becomes 110% of the previous value.

$$100\\%+10\\%=110\\%$$

So the multiplier for Fund A value first stage is 110/100.

$$\text{Fund A value first stage multiplier}=\frac{110}{100}=1.1$$

For Fund A value second stage, decrease = 10%. So the new value becomes 90% of the previous value.

$$100\\%-10\\%=90\\%$$

90% can also be written as the fraction 9/10.

$$90\\%=\frac{9}{10}$$

So the multiplier for Fund A value second stage is 90/100.

$$\text{Fund A value second stage multiplier}=\frac{90}{100}=0.9$$

So the final value of Fund A value is found by applying its combined multiplier.

$$\text{Final Fund A value}=40000\times0.99=39600$$

For Fund B value first stage, increase = 15%. So the new value becomes 115% of the previous value.

$$100\\%+15\\%=115\\%$$

So the multiplier for Fund B value first stage is 115/100.

$$\text{Fund B value first stage multiplier}=\frac{115}{100}=1.15$$

For Fund B value second stage, increase = 15%. So the new value becomes 115% of the previous value.

$$100\\%+15\\%=115\\%$$

So the multiplier for Fund B value second stage is 115/100.

$$\text{Fund B value second stage multiplier}=\frac{115}{100}=1.15$$

So the final value of Fund B value is found by applying its combined multiplier.

$$\text{Final Fund B value}=20000\times1.3225=26450$$

Now compare the two final values.

$$\text{Difference}=\left|39600-26450\right|=13150$$

So the difference between the final values is Rs. 13150.

$$\text{Difference}=13150$$

questions.stem: An output rises in the first stage by 20% and falls in the next stage by 10%. Find the net percentage change.
